claims.text: Transmission electron microscopy can investigate the thermal behavior of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles at the atomic scale.
Molecular dynamics simulations can investigate the thermal behavior of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles at the atomic scale.
The initial AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are in a random-alloy state.
The investigation covers temperatures from room temperature to high temperatures.
The molecular dynamics simulation time scale is approximately 1 ns.
Chemical short-range order is a structural mediator of the thermal behavior.
Formation of ordered clusters is a structural mediator of the thermal behavior.
AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles can be represented as a composite of a random high-entropy-alloy matrix and ordered phases.
The ordered phases have higher thermal conductivity than the random-alloy matrix.
Formation of ordered clusters and chemical short-range order increases the thermal conductivity of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
The simulation time scale and investigated temperature range bound the hypothesis.
Uncertainty arises from the accuracy of TEM characterization and molecular dynamics simulations in predicting thermal behavior.
Thermal conductivity, chemical short-range order, and ordered-cluster formation can be measured to test the hypothesis.
Failure of thermal conductivity to increase with ordered-cluster formation and short-range order would falsify the hypothesis.
